svg.text: PeerProof — attendance settled by peers
Every arrow into the contract is one transaction. Nothing between the boxes is trusted.
Attendee phone
passkey — one biometric prompt, ever
↓ PRF → BIP-39/32 → secp256k1 attest key
Participant attestation code · every 15 s
or a browser wallet / email sign-in:
one signature, same derivation, signs locally
Venue display — at the door
ephemeral beacon key
↓ holds no funds, never needs gas
Venue check-in code · every 30 s
Spent once, at check-in: proof the attendee
read a live screen in the room, rather than
knowing a secret.
another participant scans this code
the attendee scans it once, on arrival
attest(eventId, subject, epoch, code)
sent by the scanner, who must be checked in
adds to both counts · only the scanner has vouched
checkIn(eventId, beaconEpoch, beaconSig)
once per attendee, with a live venue code
the chain, not the sender, timestamps arrival
AttendanceEscrow — deployed on Monad testnet, chain 10143
deposits held by the contract · each pair attests once · counts kept per address
present = at least k attestations counted AND at least one initiated
settle() and cancelForQuorum() are permissionless · no function pays the organizer
Titles and descriptions live in a separate EventDirectory contract, which holds no money.
Every check-in and every attestation is its own transaction. Sub-second finality is Monad’s documented network
figure, not a PeerProof measurement.
